summary.title: Gamma-World: Generative Multi-Agent World Modeling Beyond Two Players

details: Video world models are almost exclusively single-agent (one action stream, one viewpoint); multi-agent simulation additionally demands consistency across agent perspectives of the same world state.
Existing multiplayer designs (dense joint attention + learned per-player ID embeddings) scale quadratically in agent count and break agent exchangeability, tying the model to a fixed roster.
Gamma-World: an action-conditioned multi-agent latent video diffusion transformer with an explicit agent axis, generating one synchronized view per agent.

Simplex Rotary Agent Encoding: a parameter-free 4D RoPE band where agents are placed at vertices of a regular simplex in rotary angle space, giving each agent a distinct phase while making all agent pairs equidistant/permutation-equivalent (agents randomly assigned to vertices from a fixed pool, so unused vertices can host extra agents at inference).

Sparse Hub Attention: direct agent-to-agent attention is masked; a few learnable per-frame hub tokens mediate all cross-agent information (agent→hub→agent), making cross-agent attention cost linear rather than quadratic in agent count.
Cosmos-Predict2.5-2B TI2V initialization; D=2048, 28 blocks, 16 heads (head dim 128), AdaLN-LoRA rank 256.

RoPE head-dim partition (t,p,h,w) = (64,32,16,16); agent band taken from the low-frequency end of the temporal band (ReRoPE-style); simplex pool V=4 with 2 active slots during training, with random vertex sampling and slot permutation.
Shared action encoder across agents (23-dim keyboard one-hot + 2-dim camera for games; 10-dim end-effector pose/gripper for robots), injected as a per-layer additive bias to self-attention inputs.
Causal student uses K=8 hub tokens per latent frame plus 24-latent-frame local attention window, bounding the KV cache.

Synchronized two-agent Minecraft trajectories generated with a SolarisEngine-inspired pipeline (scripted episodes, coordinated bots, aligned visual-action recording); four-agent scenes collected for scaling evaluation; 320x480 per view.
Real-world bimanual robotics: RealOmin-Open dataset, treating left and right arms as two agents.
Stage 1: bidirectional dense-attention teacher (flow matching), 93-frame clips for 10k iters then 189-frame clips for 6k iters.
Stage 2: block-causal multi-step student trained with Diffusion Forcing + Sparse Hub Attention, 15k iters on 93-frame clips.

Stage 3: conditional Self-Forcing / DMD distillation into a 4-step generator under autoregressive self-rollout with KV caching (400 iters, generator:critic update ratio 1:4); all stages on 32 GB200s, AdamW, no CFG at inference.
Streaming inference: per-agent KV caches plus a shared hub cache, block-by-block generation at 24 FPS.
Baselines: Multiverse-style frame/view concatenation into one visual stream; Solaris (dense joint attention + learned player ID).

Ablations: spatial vs. sequence concatenation of agent views; learned view embedding vs. Simplex Rotary Agent Encoding; dense cross-agent attention vs. Sparse Hub Attention; hub token count K in {1,8,32,128}; bidirectional vs. causal vs. distilled variants.
Metrics: FVD, FID, LPIPS, PSNR, SSIM; efficiency measured as DiT latency, self-attention latency, and analytic self-attention FLOPs for 2/4/8 agents over 24-latent rollouts.

key_findings.finding: A permutation-symmetric, parameter-free simplex rotary agent identity lets a model trained only on two agents simulate four agents zero-shot.
key_findings.evidence: Simplex vertices are provably unit-norm and equidistant (pairwise squared distance 2V/(V-1), with approximately equal separation in complex RoPE space); training samples 2 of 4 pool vertices with permuted slot order, and the same checkpoint produces synchronized four-agent rollouts without architectural change or retraining (qualitative four-agent figure).

key_findings.finding: Hub-mediated sparse cross-agent attention preserves multi-agent coupling while removing the quadratic cost of dense joint attention.
key_findings.evidence: Per-block cost drops from O(P^2 n^2 L^2) to a form linear in P; measured DiT latency, self-attention latency, and self-attention FLOPs for 2, 4, and 8 agents show substantially lower cost than dense cross-agent attention, with the gap widening as agent count grows, and ablations report Sparse Hub Attention retaining strong FVD/FID/LPIPS/PSNR/SSIM.

key_findings.finding: Treating agents as distinct but coupled token streams beats both view-concatenation and slot-embedding multi-agent designs.
key_findings.evidence: Gamma-World outperforms the Multiverse-style frame-concatenation baseline and Solaris across the reported quality/consistency metrics; ablations show sequence concatenation plus Simplex Rotary Agent Encoding improves over spatial concatenation and learned view embeddings.

key_findings.finding: Conditional Self-Forcing distillation recovers most of the bidirectional teacher's quality in a streaming-causal model.
key_findings.evidence: Bidirectional teacher: FVD 227.3 / FID 31.0 / LPIPS 0.272 / PSNR 27.7 / SSIM 0.828; multi-step causal student degrades to FVD 266.4 / FID 34.4 / PSNR 26.2; the distilled 4-step causal model reaches FVD 239.7 / FID 30.9 / LPIPS 0.273 / PSNR 26.8 while running at 24 FPS.

key_findings.finding: The same multi-agent formulation transfers from virtual games to real-world coordinated manipulation.
key_findings.evidence: Applying the model to RealOmin-Open with left and right robot arms as two agents produces future frames preserving coordinated bimanual motion and scene layout (qualitative results).
